title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — Isa 53:6; sins 'came' on Christ → Adam's on us
pass_a_gloss: GAR: Why then may I not say our sins εἰσελθεῖν into Christ, when Scripture says they came upon him? The Lord made the iniquities of us all to come or fall upon him (Isa 53:6). Likewise Adam's sin ἐλθεῖν upon us—came upon us—because we bear its reatus, that is, because it is imputed to us. So though 'enter' alone is not 'impute,' yet if the matter and place of the phrase require it, sin's entering or coming upon someone can be the same as its being imputed to him.
pass_b_english: Why then may I not say that our sins eiselthein into Christ, when Scripture says they came into Christ? The Lord made the iniquities of us all to come, or to fall upon him. Isaiah 53. 6. And likewise, that Adam's sin elthein upon us, came upon us, because we sustain its reatus, that is, because it has been imputed to us? And so although to enter simply put is not the same as to impute, yet for sin to enter, or to come upon someone, if the matter or place where the phrase is held so requires, can be the same as for that sin to be imputed to him.
source_text: Quidni ergo dixerim peccata nostra in Christum εἰσελθεῖν, cum Scriptura dicat, ea venisse in Christum? Dominus fecit venire, vel incurrere in eum iniquitates omnium nostrum. Esai. LIII. 6. Et similiter, peccatum Adae in nos ἐλθεῖν, in nos venisse, quia eius reatum sustinemus, id est, quia illud imputatum nobis est? Itaque quanquam introire simpliciter positum, non sit idem quod imputare, tamen peccatum introire, vel venire in aliquem, si res aut locus, ubi phrasis habetur, ita exigit, potest idem esse quod peccatum illud ipsi imputari.
